slides.title: A small reproduction gives us a learning signal.
slides.notes: Same 64-question monitor: 20,42,42,43,43,48,47. Latest: one gain, two losses. Improvement persists but is not monotonic. No added SFT. This is not a full MATH500 score. Fixed 255 updates and final tests continue; do not choose the best intermediate checkpoint.

slides.title: Useful practice is neither all wrong nor all right.
slides.notes: Rewards minus their question's mean: allzero and allone groups give zero. Mixing easy and impossible questions does not fix that. Curriculum could keep practice within reach. Do not claim50percent success is always optimal or mixed rewards guarantee learning.

slides.title: Existing skill needs a usable interface.
slides.notes: Same base and short chat-trained weights in both rows; test prompt alone changes. Full500 checker and3000token cap match. No-template training repeats added9 and1. SFT is optional. For RLMs distinguish knowing Python from knowing our API and choosing useful subtasks.

slides.title: Teach the interface, then practice useful choices.
slides.notes: Proposed sequence, not established fact. Measure skills first; do not assume the model lacks Python. Example: pass employer name to the next lookup. Gradually remove hints; retain some earlier practice. Related RLM work already trains on demonstrations; novelty needs a sharper test.

slides.title: Prior work supports the ingredients, not our sequence.
slides.notes: DAPO is adaptive filtering, not proof of an easy-to-hard curriculum. RLMs already have demonstration training and a separate RL transfer result. R1 cold start is optional, as R1-Zero shows. Our possible contribution is which skills, order, and transfer, not SFT before RL itself.

slides.title: A portfolio of small experiments, not one settled story.
slides.notes: User favors breadth. Curriculum is one hypothesis, not the conclusion. Separate missing skills, teaching order, exploration and repair. Freeze helpers for early comparisons. Measure each setup before and after RL at matched budgets. Small screens guide independent repeats; retain failures.
